name: Eiffel Tower
description: The wrought-iron icon designed by Gustave Eiffel for the 1889 World's Fair. Once the tallest structure on Earth, it now welcomes nearly seven million visitors a year and stands at the heart of Paris.
fact: On hot days the iron expands and the tower can grow up to 15 cm taller.

name: Burj Khalifa
description: The tallest building in the world, soaring 828 metres above Dubai. Designed by Adrian Smith, it holds more than half a dozen world records and inspired by the geometry of a desert flower.
fact: Lifts inside the Burj Khalifa travel at 10 metres per second, among the fastest on the planet.

name: Tokyo Skytree
description: Japan's tallest structure and the world's tallest free-standing tower. Skytree blends ancient pagoda silhouettes with cutting-edge anti-seismic engineering.
fact: Its height of 634 m reads as 'mu-sa-shi' in Japanese, the historical name of the Tokyo region.

name: Shanghai Tower
description: A 128-storey spiral that twists 120 degrees as it climbs. Its double-skin facade saves an estimated 25 percent on heating and cooling.
fact: Shanghai Tower hosts the world's highest observation deck inside a building, 561 metres up.

name: Petronas Towers
description: Iconic twins linked by a sky-bridge at the 41st floor. Designed by César Pelli, their floor plan echoes the geometric patterns of Islamic art.
fact: When they opened in 1998 they were the tallest buildings in the world for six straight years.

name: One World Trade Center
description: The tallest building in the Western Hemisphere stands as the symbolic centerpiece of Lower Manhattan's renewal, topping out at exactly 1776 feet.
fact: The 1776-foot height is a tribute to the year of American independence.

name: CN Tower
description: For more than three decades the tallest free-standing structure in the world. Today it offers a glass floor 342 metres above ground and the heart-stopping EdgeWalk.
fact: Visitors can walk hands-free along a 1.5 m ledge at 356 metres of altitude.

name: Taipei 101
description: An 8-segment pagoda stack engineered to ride out the typhoons and earthquakes of the Pacific Rim. A 660-tonne golden damper hangs at the top.
fact: Its tuned mass damper sphere is the largest on Earth and visible to the public.

name: Empire State Building
description: Built in just 410 days during the Great Depression, the Empire State stood as the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years.
fact: Lightning strikes the building roughly 25 times every year.

name: Elizabeth Tower (Big Ben)
description: The four-faced chiming clock at the north end of the Palace of Westminster. The name Big Ben technically belongs to the largest of its bells.
fact: The clock's hands are made of copper and weigh together more than 300 kilograms.

name: Tokyo Tower
description: An orange-and-white homage to Paris that became Japan's symbol of post-war recovery. Still serves as a broadcast antenna and observation deck.
fact: Tokyo Tower stands 13 metres taller than the Eiffel Tower it was modelled on.

name: Willis Tower
description: Originally the Sears Tower, it pioneered the bundled-tube structural system and ruled the world skyline for 25 years.
fact: Its Skydeck features glass boxes hanging 412 metres above the city streets.

name: Lotte World Tower
description: Korea's tallest building tapers gracefully toward a luminous lantern crown inspired by traditional ceramics and calligraphy.
fact: Its observation deck Seoul Sky has glass floors that look 478 metres straight down.

name: Ping An Finance Center
description: The fourth-tallest building in the world, sheathed in 1700 tonnes of stainless steel that resist Shenzhen's typhoon-force winds.
fact: Its Free Sky observation deck is the highest open-air viewing area in China.

name: Ostankino Tower
description: A Soviet engineering landmark that was the world's tallest free-standing structure for nine years and still anchors Moscow's broadcasting.
fact: Its design relies on 149 steel cables tensioned inside the concrete shaft.

name: Space Needle
description: Built for the 1962 World's Fair, its UFO-shaped top deck now spins slowly above a glass floor giving 360-degree views of Mount Rainier and Puget Sound.
fact: The original sketch was drawn on a placemat in a Seattle coffee shop.

name: Berliner Fernsehturm
description: The tallest structure in Germany. Its mirrored sphere catches the sun in a cross shape, jokingly nicknamed 'the Pope's revenge'.
fact: Its rotating restaurant completes one full turn every 30 minutes.

name: Eureka Tower
description: Crowned with 24-karat gold-plated glass, Eureka Tower hosts the Skydeck 88, one of the highest viewing platforms in the southern hemisphere.
fact: Its glass cube 'The Edge' slides three metres outside the building before turning transparent.

name: Two International Finance Centre
description: A tapered finance tower whose 88 storeys reference the Chinese number for prosperity. Headquarters of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
fact: The film Lara Croft: Tomb Raider was partly shot atop its mast.

name: Burj Al Arab
description: A sail-shaped silhouette rising from a man-made island. Often described as the world's most luxurious hotel, it became Dubai's first global icon.
fact: A helipad on the 28th floor has hosted tennis matches and a Formula 1 driver's stunt.

name: Spinnaker Tower
description: Designed to evoke the sails of Portsmouth's maritime history, Spinnaker Tower offers views over the Solent and the Isle of Wight.
fact: Its top platform features a glass floor that always slightly bends underfoot.

name: 30 St Mary Axe (Gherkin)
description: Iconic 'Gherkin' silhouette in the City of London, designed by Norman Foster with a diagonal lattice facade.
fact: Its diagonal grid lets it use 50% less energy than a conventional tower of the same size.

name: 20 Fenchurch (Walkie-Talkie)
description: Top-heavy curved skyscraper crowned by London's largest public sky garden across three storeys.
fact: Its concave south facade once focused sunlight enough to melt plastic on parked cars below.

name: One Canada Square
description: Postmodern centerpiece of Canary Wharf, originally Britain's tallest building at completion.
fact: The pyramid roof beacon flashes about 57600 times every year as an aircraft warning.

name: Federation Tower
description: Tallest of the Moscow City complex, with two needle-like spires crowning a glass-and-steel core.
fact: Construction began in 2003 and stalled multiple times before finally topping out in 2017.

name: Lakhta Center
description: Tallest building in Europe and the world's northernmost supertall, rising over the Gulf of Finland.
fact: Its spiral form rotates roughly 90 degrees from the base to the crown.

name: Mercury City Tower
description: First building in Europe to top 300 metres, sheathed in striking amber-coloured glass.
fact: Mercury City held the European height record from 2012 until 2017.

name: Commerzbank Tower
description: World's first ecological skyscraper, with sky gardens spiraling up its triangular core.
fact: Its central glass atrium runs the full 56-storey height of the building.

name: Messeturm
description: Held Europe's height record before Commerzbank Tower, capped by a striking pyramid crown.
fact: Its red granite facade includes more than 8000 individually cut stone panels.

name: Torre Glòries
description: Geyser-inspired bullet of glass and aluminium designed by Jean Nouvel, a Barcelona icon.
fact: By night some 4500 LED devices paint its surface in shifting colours.

name: Torre de Cristal
description: Tallest of Madrid's Cuatro Torres business cluster, finished with a glass crown of inclined panels.
fact: Its sky garden on the 32nd floor is one of Europe's highest indoor gardens.

name: Jin Mao Tower
description: Postmodern reinterpretation of a Chinese pagoda by SOM and an anchor of the Lujiazui skyline.
fact: The number 8, considered lucky in China, is built into nearly every dimension of the tower.

name: Oriental Pearl Tower
description: Distinctive multi-sphere TV tower on the Pudong skyline, an emblem of modern Shanghai.
fact: Its rotating restaurant orbits 267 metres above the Huangpu River.

name: International Commerce Centre
description: Tallest building in Hong Kong, crowned by the Sky100 indoor observation deck.
fact: Light shows on its facade form one of the largest LED displays mounted on a building.

name: Bank of China Tower
description: I.M. Pei's iconic angular landmark, designed to evoke segmented bamboo growth.
fact: It was the first building outside the United States to exceed 305 metres.

name: Mahanakhon
description: Distinctive 'collapsing pixel' facade making the tower look like an unfinished cube.
fact: Its glass observation tray sticks 4.5 metres beyond the building's edge.

name: Baiyoke Tower II
description: Tallest hotel in Thailand, crowned by a 360-degree rooftop revolving observation deck.
fact: Its rainbow-coloured night lighting changes its dominant hue every five minutes.

name: Marina Bay Sands
description: Three towers crowned by the boat-shaped SkyPark with the world's longest elevated pool.
fact: Its rooftop infinity pool floats 191 metres above the streets of Singapore.

name: Tanjong Pagar Centre
description: Tallest building in Singapore, mixing offices, residences and a luxury hotel.
fact: Its height is officially capped by airspace restrictions over the city centre.

name: China Zun (CITIC Tower)
description: Tallest building in Beijing, shaped after the ancient Chinese 'zun' ritual vessel.
fact: Its base and crown widen out, creating a unique waist-shaped silhouette.

name: Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre
description: Among the world's tallest buildings, with four soft setback transitions and a tapered crown.
fact: Its express elevators travel about 20 metres per second, near the world's fastest.

name: Chrysler Building
description: Briefly the world's tallest building before the Empire State, defined by its sunburst stainless-steel crown.
fact: Its hidden spire was raised in just 90 minutes to claim the world height record.

name: Salesforce Tower
description: Tallest building in San Francisco, crowned by a 1.5 million-LED public art installation.
fact: Its earthquake-resistant foundation reaches some 90 metres down into bedrock.

name: Wilshire Grand Center
description: Tallest building in Los Angeles, crowned by a sweeping sail and a slender spire.
fact: Its concrete pour for the foundation was the largest single pour in United States history.

name: 432 Park Avenue
description: One of the slimmest supertall residential towers in the world, dominating the Manhattan skyline.
fact: Each window is exactly three metres on a side, arranged in a perfect grid.

name: 30 Hudson Yards
description: Anchor of the Hudson Yards development with the highest outdoor observation deck in the Western Hemisphere.
fact: Its triangular Edge platform juts 24 metres out from the side of the building.

name: Makkah Royal Clock Tower
description: Anchor of the Abraj Al Bait complex, sporting the largest clock face in the world.
fact: Its main clock dial measures 43 metres across and is visible from 17 kilometres away.

name: Kingdom Centre
description: Iconic parabolic-arch silhouette of Riyadh, with a glass sky bridge spanning the top opening.
fact: Its illuminated arch is among the most recognised buildings in the entire Gulf region.

name: Capital Gate
description: Officially the most-leaning man-made tower in the world at 18 degrees, exceeding the Tower of Pisa.
fact: Each floor cantilevers 30 to 140 cm beyond the floor below to create the lean.

name: Etihad Towers Tower 2
description: Tallest of the five Etihad Towers, defining the modern Abu Dhabi Corniche skyline.
fact: Its 74th-floor observation lounge has been used as a James Bond film location.
